quarterly_data.signal: Eli Lilly's 10-K revenue mix for 2025: net product revenue was $60,958 million (2024: $40,748 million) and collaboration and other revenue $4,221 million (2024: $4,295 million). By therapeutic area, cardiometabolic health revenue was $33,864 million in the U.S. and $14,357 million outside the U.S. (2024: $21,850 million and $7,671 million), oncology $5,352 million and $4,024 million, immunology $2,964 million and $2,283 million, and neuroscience $997 million and $394 million. Trulicity revenue was $2,914 million in the U.S. (2024: $3,694 million) and $1,362 million outside the U.S.; Taltz $2,333 million in the U.S. and $1,230 million outside the U.S. Rest-of-world revenue was $6,057 million (2024: $4,271 million).
quarterly_data.figure: net product revenue $60,958 million (vs $40,748 million); collaboration and other $4,221 million; cardiometabolic U.S. $33,864 million / outside U.S. $14,357 million; oncology $5,352 million / $4,024 million; immunology $2,964 million / $2,283 million; neuroscience $997 million / $394 million; Trulicity U.S. $2,914 million; Taltz U.S. $2,333 million

quarterly_data.signal: Eli Lilly's 10-K cost and investment lines for 2025: research and development was $13,337 million (up 21%), of which early-stage $4,881 million and late-stage $8,456 million; marketing, selling and administrative $11,094 million (up 29%); acquired in-process research and development $2,910 million (down 11%). Net cash provided by operating activities was $16,813 million (2024: $8,818 million), and expenditures for long-lived assets were $8,672 million (2024: $5,561 million). Lilly says it is continuing the significant expansion of its manufacturing capabilities and substantial investment in long-term supply agreements to fortify supply and support its ability to meet anticipated demand, and that it depends on China-based suppliers for portions of its supply chain, including integral chemical synthesis, reagents, starting materials and ingredients.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D $13,337 million (+21%); marketing, selling and administrative $11,094 million (+29%); acquired IPR&D $2,910 million; operating cash flow $16,813 million (vs $8,818 million); expenditures for long-lived assets $8,672 million (vs $5,561 million)
